climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Riesling, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Gewürztraminer and Pinot Noir fully without cooking off their freshness.
Riesling, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Pinot Gris is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Most rain falls while the vines grow. Damp leaves invite mildew and rot, so growers spray more and pick carefully.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water. Clay holds water well but drains poorly. It stays cool, which slows ripening and keeps acidity up.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.
